subject: POC stitch plan — SDK routes, streaming & function-calling fallbacks
messages:
From: Marta Alvarez <marta@stitchworks.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 1 Sep 2026 09:02:00 -0700
Subject: POC stitch plan — next steps & tech clarifications

Thanks for the demo this morning — Daniel and I walked through the recording and have a few follow-ups so we can scope the POC properly. High-level asks below; we attached our draft scope doc (stitchworks-poc-scope.pdf).

Recap / asks:
- Success criteria we care about: 95th percentile latency <= 400ms for single-turn queries; bulk embedding recall >= 92% (baseline attached).
- Integration: we plan to use your JS SDK for streaming generation in our preview UI, and call functions (tool-calling) to surface structured matches from our index. Need confirmation on supported function schema and streaming route names.
- Fallbacks & routing: if GPU capacity is constrained, we need a deterministic fallback path to a lower-cost model (preferably same API routes).
- Instrumentation: we need per-request IDs in the response headers for tracing and a simple event we can emit on partial chunks.

Next steps we propose:
1) We schedule a 30-min technical kickoff with engineering to map API routes and confirm SDK examples.
2) Red-team/security will run a short questionnaire (we attached a CSV of initial questions).
3) Agree on ownership for rollout tasks and an acceptance checklist.

Can you confirm whether streaming + function-calling is supported in your Dedicated routing policies, and whether SDK has a built-in fallback helper we can call?

Thanks — looking to kick this off next week if possible.

Best,
Marta Alvarez
Head of Product, StitchWorks

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: POC stitch plan — next steps & tech clarifications

Marta — thanks for the clear recap and the scope doc. Appreciate the latency/recall targets; those help us size the Dedicated pool for the trial. Replying inline below and attaching a short integration outline (redwood-poc-integration-outline.md).

On your asks:
- Streaming + function-calling: supported. Streaming route is /v1/generate/stream and supports chunked JSON with chunk_id + request_id in each chunk header. Function-calling follows the JSON-RPC-like schema we showed; SDK helpers validate schema before sending.
- Fallbacks & routing: yes — we have a routing policy layer. You can pin a primary model and specify an ordered list of fallbacks (model_variant v1 -> quantized v1 -> lightweight v2). The request header X-Routing-Policy indicates which tier served the request. We'll include an example policy in the outline.
- Instrumentation: we emit x-request-id and x-model-variant headers. For streaming, each chunk includes chunk_seq and request_id. SDK exposes an onChunk callback where you can forward instrumentation events.

Proposed POC timeline (high level):
- Day 0 (Kickoff): technical mapping + confirm security questionnaire scope.
- Week 1: SDK quickstart + sample streaming integration in a sandbox.
- Week 2–3: Run 3k requests/day benchmark and embedding recall validation.
- Week 4: Acceptance window and handoff to product.

Ownership (proposal):
- Redwood: Marcus (technical lead), Vanessa (ops / routing & SLA), SDK engineer on call.
- StitchWorks: Daniel (engineer lead), Marta (product success owner).

Acceptance checklist (draft):
- SDK stream sample working in your sandbox with <400ms 95p latency for single-turn demo cases.
- Function calls return well-formed JSON that maps to your index schema.
- Fallback policy exercised under simulated capacity drop.
- Security questionnaire items answered (we'll iterate with Priyom).

I'll host a 30-min kickoff on Friday 9/3 at 10:00am PT — does that work?

Marcus Lin
Sr. Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Marta — quick technical notes / clarifications from infra & SDK perspective (replying to Marcus's plan):

- SDK routes & names:
  * Streaming generation: POST /v1/generate/stream (websocket and SSE supported in JS SDK).
  * Function-calling endpoint is the same /v1/generate with body.function_schema present; SDK sets mode: "function".
  * Embeddings: POST /v1/embeddings (batch + single).

- Streaming semantics: partial chunks are valid JSON objects; final chunk includes "done": true. Use request_id to correlate. We recommend a small client-side buffer (50–100ms) to avoid choppy UI rendering.

- Fallback testing plan: we can provide a small traffic-shaping script that simulates node drain and exercises fallback chain. It logs X-Routing-Policy changes so you can validate deterministic behavior.

- Quantization/latency tradeoff: if you need lower unit cost during heavy load, we recommend quantized fallback variant (q8_0). We will provide recommended default config for your workload distribution.

- Security questionnaire: we'll take the CSV and start populating fields; if you need encryption-at-rest proof, we can attach KMS docs during the kickoff.

I'll join the Friday kickoff and bring a short demo (5–7 minutes) of the streaming sample + fallback test.

— Priyom
Principal Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
priyom_das@redwood.com
